Text fit (first-reader point 6): 'fills' in 08-1 has about 6 px of right padding, against about 18 px on the left. 'his' in 08-3, 'on' in 08-5 and 'ready.' in the balloon sit near their borders, but every glyph is fully inside its box and legible. These are tight, but not defects.

Typography (point 7): the gap in 'We' ll' comes from the monospace font. The same apostrophe appears throughout the comic ('We'll' on 06, 'Let's' and 'That's' on 07, 'I've' on 05), so it is consistent house lettering and readable. Ending a line after a middle dot ('app ·') follows the same pattern as the labels on pages 05-06 ('prescribing ·', 'current vitals ·'). The apparent indent on 'is notified' in 08-5 and 08-6 is the narrow, centred monospace 'i', not a leading space (the textColumns have trailing spaces only).

Tube caps (point 8): the 08-2 art shows purple caps and the 08-3 art shows red caps, both on the tube she holds and on the rack. This is an artwork matter, not lettering. No text names a colour or claims it is the same tube. In a clinic lab, different tests use tubes with different coloured caps, so the mismatch reads as plausible and does not change the meaning. I do not count it as a lettering issue. The parent may pass it to an artwork review if exact prop continuity is wanted.

Unnamed woman in 08-6 (point 9): the first reader saw page 08 alone. In the comic, pages 01-07 have established Meera at this reception desk, in this blue kurta with this braid. The caption refers to 'the clinic' on purpose, because the notification goes to the clinic through Welbuk Practice. Acceptable.

Timeline against pages 06-07: 07-4 shows Ravi walking away from the clinic. 'Meanwhile' reads as 'while he heads off'. 'Later that day, Ravi gives his samples at the clinic lab', with his bag on his lap, shows he came back the same day, which is the decision confirmed in Request 4. The 06-2 label 'intelligent prescribing · ... · labs' sets up NEW PRESCRIPTION and LAB ORDER. 08-4's 'Results ready' and its evening setting at home mark a later day.

Reading the page cold: top row left to right; the wide middle panel, caption at top left and then the balloon at top right; then the tall bottom-left panel, caption and then label; then the two stacked right panels, top to bottom. In every panel the white caption sits above or to the left of the teal label, so each panel reads caption first, then label.
The only speech is in 08-3, and it shares that row only with its own caption, so a skip is unlikely. The two RESULTS READY labels sit in separate panels.

Her promise 'We'll let you know when your results are ready' leads directly into 'Results ready: Ravi is notified.' at home in evening light.
The same 'is notified' pattern moves on to Dr. Ananya, at her desk and in the clothes from pages 05-06.
Stacked panels with matching captions: the doctor on Welbuk Care, then the clinic on Welbuk Practice, both showing the same check card.

With the chain of notifications complete, the caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' and the train window open a clearly marked, conditional jump into the future on the vision page the user kept.
